description: Gaia Saviors is a Cairo-based team competing in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We build practical solutions using NASA data, AI, Earth observation, and software engineering. Our focus is the MODIS & VIIRS Hot Spots challenge, covering fire detection, tracking, data harmonization, and 3D visualization. We welcome teammates interested in GIS, remote sensing, AI/ML, data science, frontend, 3D, and scientific research.
summary: EmberEye is a web platform for exploring a consistent record of active-fire detections from NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS products. It normalizes sensor and satellite metadata, removes duplicate detections, and uses the 2012–2022 overlap to calibrate pre-2012 MODIS activity into explicitly labeled VIIRS-equivalent estimates. These are model-dependent estimates, not observations from VIIRS. Users can choose a region and date range, browse daily and monthly fire-activity calendars and a map, compare time series and climatology, inspect fire episodes, and export filtered results. The current offline demo contains real NASA FIRMS detections for the Nile Delta and clearly labeled deterministic synthetic demo data for the other five preset regions. EmberEye exposes provenance and uncertainty and is intended for research and exploration, not operational fire alerts or forecasts.
details:
EmberEye addresses the challenge’s need for a comparable burning-activity record and a web app for selecting an area and time range, exploring patterns, and downloading results. It ingests NASA FIRMS active-fire products: MODIS Collection 6.1 from Terra and Aqua, and 375 m VIIRS from Suomi-NPP (historical), NOAA-20, and NOAA-21. The pipeline maps records to a common schema, keeps sensor/product provenance and provisional NRT status, and applies sensor-specific duplicate suppression. An optional NASA GIBS MODIS Terra thermal-anomaly layer and public basemaps provide map context.

For the harmonized series, VIIRS is the reference. During the 2012–2022 overlap, EmberEye fits month-of-year transfer factors on daytime, non-static detections and evaluates them with leave-one-year-out validation. It uses those factors to estimate pre-2012 MODIS activity in VIIRS-equivalent units, with uncertainty intervals; the estimate is explicitly not presented as a historical VIIRS observation. Native VIIRS is used in the VIIRS era, and overlapping satellites are not simply summed. The app also provides daily/monthly calendars, an interactive map and date scrubber, time-series and climatology views, fire-episode summaries, area-of-interest selection, and CSV/GeoJSON exports.

The v1.0.8 offline snapshot contains 171,855 real FIRMS detections for the Nile Delta; its other five preset regions contain deterministic synthetic demo records. On that Nile Delta snapshot, annual pooled leave-one-year-out MAPE was 7.03%, mean bias was −2.01%, and the empirical 95% prediction interval was [−18.15%, +12.21%]. Those are snapshot- and annual-aggregation-specific diagnostics, not a global accuracy guarantee; monthly and weekly MAPE were 33.77% and 83.52%. NRT observations are provisional. The app is a research and exploration prototype, not a fire forecast, operational alert system, or substitute for official incident information.

The implementation uses Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL/SQLite, React, TypeScript, MapLibre GL JS, Apache ECharts, and Docker Compose.
